newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan, U.S. condemn attack on schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan, U.S. condemn attack on schoolgirls.

text.p: The killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier on Thursday came against the backdrop of high Israeli-Arab tensions over Jewish settlement policy.
Following are excerpts of comments by political leaders and witnesses to the attack on a border tract known to Israelis as "The Island of Peace":

"Today along the normally peaceful border between Israel and Jordan, we have seen an inexcusable and tragic act of violence against schoolchildren. I condemn this act in the strongest possible terms."

"This was a wicked attack that caused a terrible tragedy. We're talking about the murder of innocent girls who were on a field trip...I think this event manifests what I have been saying for a long time, that the mentality of certain elements who sanctify violence and are willing to employ violences poses the biggest threat to the peace process."

-- Israeli Education Minister Zvulun Hammer, referring to a letter from King Hussein to Netanyahu earlier this week warning of possible violence over Israel's plans to build 6,500 more homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem:
"Perhaps the conclusion is that the King must hold his tongue so that a soldier doesn't take his words to mean more than he indended."
-- Jordan's King Hussein expressed his "sorrow at the tragic loss of life of the innocent" and added:
"This is something that is aimed I feel at me, at my children, at the people of Jordan...and the Jordanian army."
Asked about Israeli criticism of his letter to Netanyahu, the monarch said:
"It was fully in my responsibility to warn that we have come too far."

"Who knows...how many of these gun-toting lunatics are waiting for the green light in the form a remark in which Israel is described the way it is being described today." Levy said he was not referring to King Hussein's letter.
-- Israeli Labour party leader Shimon Peres:
"We hoped this would be an island of peace, and it was. I hope it will will not become an island of blood."
-- Hila Ivri, a 14-year-old wounded in the attack:
"I saw the gunmen. He held his gun. He was shooting, and then he started shooting again...He was a bad guy with big eyes."
